Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh + 40 fps cap is the sweet spot for this game on Deck, delivering smooth web-swinging and combat without the GPU struggling to hit 60. Rendering at 1024x640 with FSR upscale gives a noticeably sharper image than the MaxBattery profile while keeping the frame rate locked.

profiles.Summary: Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered is a demanding open-world action game that runs on the Steam Deck with Platinum-tier Proton compatibility, but its PC requirements (recommended GTX 1060 6GB) push the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU hard, requiring lower settings and FSR upscaling to maintain stable frame rates. Expect 30–45 fps depending on settings, with open-world traversal and busy combat scenes being the most taxing scenarios.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck player reports were found; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements versus the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class). On first launch, check frame rate during open-world web-swinging — if it dips below 30 fps consistently on the Optimal profile, drop to MaxBattery settings or lower render resolution further.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 and let FSR upscale to 1280x800; the reduced GPU clock and 8 W TDP cap keep temperatures and power draw low for extended sessions. Keep crowd density and shadow quality at Low as these are the biggest performance drains in open-world traversal.

KnownIssues: Ray tracing options should be disabled — the Deck GPU cannot handle them at any playable frame rate.
Web-swinging through dense city areas can cause frame rate dips even at lower settings.
No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from hardware specs and PC requirements.
Initial shader compilation on first launch may cause stuttering until the cache is built up.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At full 15 W TDP and max GPU clock the Deck can push close to a consistent 45 fps in most areas, though heavy traversal scenes may dip to the low 40s; a 45 fps cap prevents the GPU from chasing unachievable higher frames and wastes less power. Battery life is short at this setting, so plug in or plan for under 1.5 hours per charge.

Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh rate with a 40 fps cap is the sweet spot for this game on OLED — it feels smooth and stable while medium settings keep the city looking great. FSR 2 Balanced at 1024x640 gives a clean upscaled image with minimal ghosting during web-swinging.

profiles.Summary: Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered runs well on the Steam Deck OLED under Proton, achieving a stable 30-40 fps with low-to-medium settings and FSR upscaling. The game is demanding for the Deck's GPU, sitting above the minimum spec class, so lower settings and upscaling are essential for smooth play.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck–specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs relative to the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class) and ProtonDB's platinum rating indicating it runs well under Proton. On your first run, check the frame counter during open-world web-swinging in Manhattan — that is the hardest scene — and drop to the Optimal or Max Battery profile if frame rate dips below your cap consistently.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 keeps the GPU load manageable; the 8 W TDP cap and fixed GPU clock extend battery significantly. Crowd density and shadow quality are the biggest performance levers in this game.

KnownIssues: No Deck-specific player reports found; profiles are estimated from PC requirements and hardware comparisons.
The game is GPU-heavy and may struggle in dense open-world areas of Manhattan at higher settings.
Ray tracing options (if enabled) will severely tank performance and should be disabled.
High-quality texture streaming may cause stutters due to shared VRAM/RAM on the 16 GB unified memory pool.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At full 15 W TDP and maximum GPU clock the Deck can push toward 60 fps in less demanding areas, but expect dips to the mid-40s in busy Manhattan streets — a 60 fps cap is set as the ceiling, not a guarantee. Drop Crowd Density to Low and Reflection Quality to Low to keep the frame rate from collapsing during web-swinging sequences.
